validity.researcher_notes: STANDING CONTEXT: wiki_citations.json is empty for this scope (gem.wiki 403'd the harvester all run) and the row's [ref] cells are all MISSING_REF, so there was nothing pre-existing to re-verify -- this is fresh research from the open web, per the scope note. gem.wiki itself also 403'd my own WebFetch attempt (Cloudflare), so I never saw the wiki page; not cited per standing rules regardless. EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed. SNGPL's own site (the utility that would own/operate this exact asset) publishes a live 'Province-Wise Transmission Breakup' page under What We Do > Transmission System listing 'SUI - MULTAN (24-inch): 288.06 km' under the Punjab section -- an exact match to GEM's LengthKnown=288.06/Diameter=24in to 2 decimal places. SNGPL's 'History of SNGPL' page (About Us) independently corroborates that SNGPL acquired/operates the Sui-Multan trunk system from its 1963-64 incorporation ('took over the existing Sui-Multan System with 217 miles of 16 inch and 80 miles of 10 inch diameter pipelines' from PIDC) -- this describes the ORIGINAL 1950s/60s pipe (16in/10in), not today's 24in main line, which is consistent with decades of replacement/looping (SNGPL's roster already shows three later loop lines at 30in/18in/36in, P4091/P4097/P4098). The 217mi(16in)/80mi(10in) 1963 figures do not contradict today's 24in/288.06km spec once understood as different eras of the same evolving system -- no conflict, just history vs current-state. CLASSIFICATION: correct. This is explicitly filed by SNGPL itself under 'Transmission System' (a province-crossing trunk line, Balochistan gas field to Punjab demand centers), not a gathering/feeder line -- transmission is right. FUEL: Gas -- trivially correct (SNGPL = Sui Northern GAS Pipelines Ltd; the Sui field is a gas field). DUPLICATE: checked against the full 63-row roster. No other row is plausibly the same physical segment as P4090 -- P4091 (30in/313.78km), P4097 (18in/256.82km, from Bhong), and P4098 (36in/213.68km, from Bhong) are parallel loop lines of DIFFERENT diameter, and SNGPL's own breakdown table independently lists 24in/30in/36in as separate lines in the Punjab section (matching P4090/P4091/P4098's exact lengths), confirming these are genuinely four distinct pipes along one corridor, not duplicates/relabels of each other. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=SNGPL 100% -- confirmed (it is definitionally SNGPL's own transmission asset per SNGPL's own site). StartLocation/StartState=Sui/Balochistan is the one soft concern, detailed above -- the 288.06km figure itself is a Punjab-only sub-length of a three-province 24-inch line, so the Sui/Balochistan endpoint label is nominal (brand/corridor name) rather than what the recorded length actually measures; GEM is internally inconsistent on this convention across the four related rows (P4090/P4091 label from 'Sui' while P4097/P4098 label from 'Bhong', Punjab, even though all four lengths are Punjab-segment-only per SNGPL's table). SPEC: Length=288.06km and Diameter=24in are an exact, high-precision match to SNGPL's own official current network data -- as strong a spec confirmation as this project gets, short of a second fully independent (non-SNGPL) source. STATUS: 'operating' is reasonable -- the line appears in SNGPL's live, current 'Transmission System' inventory (not an archived/historical page), so it is presently in service. TIER NOTE: both citations trace to one origin (SNGPL) -- I could not reach a second independent source within this run: Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo/Ecosia/Mojeek/Startpage were all blocked or CAPTCHA-gated to WebFetch, and the session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before I could use it for this row. Given SNGPL is the actual owner/operator publishing its own asset register, I'm confident in the values themselves (tier=medium, not fabricated, not GEM-derived) but flag the corroboration count honestly as single-origin.
